newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates unchanged after M3, Buba.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates unchanged after M3, Buba.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were virtually unchanged on Thursday but dealers noted some upward pressure on receding hopes of an early cut of the German repo.

"The latest German M3 figure was at the top of the range of expectations, which is not very good for the market," said one dealer. He expected it could be two months before the Bundesbank might lower the repo rate, the main tool for guiding the overnight money market rate.
Last week market players speculated that the repo could be trimmed after Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said Germany could not ignore recent German jobless figures.
"The positive sentiment has been pushed forward a little, partly because of the M3 data," said the dealer.
German money supply growth in December was 7.9 percent versus 8.0 percent in November, while the market had been expecting an average of 7.6 percent.
Early on Thursday afternoon the Bundesbank said it had left interest rates unchanged and had set the next two weekly repos at a fixed 3.00 percent.
Dealers said they expected the special advances rate, the Dutch equivalent of the German repo, to remain at 2.50 percent when the Dutch central bank sets a new pact at 1500 GMT.
The guilder remained weak against he mark, but dealers said the current rate did not demand a rise in the special advances.
The guilder was trading at 112.3125 per 100 marks versus 112.32 on Wednesday.
